newsitem.title: UK: Safeway leads food retail sector lower.
newsitem.headline: Safeway leads food retail sector lower.

text.p: Shares in major UK food retailers continued to sink on Wednesday amid worries about the group's prospects and expectations of additional broker downgrades, dealers said.
At 0854 GMT, shares in Tesco Plc were down for the fourth straight session, falling 2p to 329-1/2, the lowest price since mid-November.
Shares is ASDA Plc and Safeway Plc slipped to their lowest levels in four months, easing 3/4p to 111-1/4 and 3p to 343-1/2, respectively. Shares in J Sainsbury lost 1-1/2p to 313.
The sector has been under heavy pressure in recent weeks as worries about profit margins and sales were raised.
Most recently, Safeway issued a cautious statement, warning that profits could be hit by a slowdown in sales.
Several analysts have cut their earnings estimates on companies in the sector and there was talk of more downgrades.
There was a report that brokerages ABN AMRO Hoare Govett and BZW were preparing downgrades on Tesco.
An ABN AMRO food retail analyst said he hadn't cut his estimates, but wouldn't say if he was planning to do so. BZW couldn't immediately be reached for comment.
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson was said to be negative on Sainsbury, but the brokerage wouldn't comment on its stance on the stock.
